title_en: Shenzhen Commercial Bank, Bao'an Sub-branch v. Hunan Changlian Xingchang Group Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Minxin Industrial Co., Ltd., Guangdong Jinhuiyuan Investment Guarantee Co., Ltd., Northwest Yaao Information Technology Co., Ltd., Wuzhong Instrument Group Co., Ltd., and Shenzhen Guo'an Accounting Firm Co., Ltd. — dispute over guarantee contract for return of funds
ruling_gist_en: Whether a financial institution should bear liability for compensation to a creditor for issuing a false capital verification certificate shall depend on whether the creditor's loss was caused by reasonable reliance on or use of the false capital verification certificate issued by the financial institution, i.e., whether there is a causal relationship between the creditor's loss and the act of the financial institution issuing the false capital verification certificate. If there is no causal relationship between the creditor's loss and the act of the financial institution issuing the false capital verification certificate, then the financial institution shall not be liable for the creditor's loss arising from the issuance of the false capital verification certificate.

full_text_en:
Shenzhen Commercial Bank, Bao'an Sub-branch v. Hunan Changlian Xingchang Group Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Minxin Industrial Co., Ltd., Guangdong Jinhuiyuan Investment Guarantee Co., Ltd., Northwest Ya'Ao Information Technology Co., Ltd., Wuzhong Instrument Group Co., Ltd., and Shenzhen Guo'an Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. — dispute over return of funds and guarantee contracts

[Ruling Summary]

Whether a financial institution should bear compensation liability for losses of a creditor arising from issuing false capital verification documents depends on whether the creditor's loss was caused by reasonable reliance on or use of such false documents issued by the financial institution, i.e., whether there is a causal relationship between the creditor's loss and the act of the financial institution issuing false capital verification documents. If there is no causal relationship between the creditor's loss and the act of the financial institution issuing false capital verification documents, the financial institution shall not be liable for compensating the creditor's loss.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2007) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 26

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Shenzhen Commercial Bank, Bao'an Sub-branch, domiciled at: 1/F, CTS Hotel, No. 21 District Chuangye Road, Bao'an District, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

Responsible Person: Xu Bo, Sub-branch Manager.

Agent ad litem: Ge Xiaoxiang, employee of Shenzhen Commercial Bank.

Agent ad litem: Wang Zhaohui, lawyer at Beijing Chuangtian Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Hunan Changlian Xingchang Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Changlian, Yunxi District, Yueyang City, Hunan Province.

Legal Representative: Yi Jianbo, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Yang Weihua, lawyer at Beijing Huiyue Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Tang Minhuang, lawyer at Beijing Dishi Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Shenzhen Minxin Industrial Co., Ltd., domiciled at: 5th Floor, Building 24, Science and Technology Industrial Park, Shenwan Avenue, Nanshan District, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Mao Hua, Chairman of the Board.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Guangdong Jinhuiyuan Investment Guarantee Co., Ltd., domiciled at: 26/F, Building B, Changxing Building, Huaqiang North Road, Futian District, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Yuming, General Manager of the Company.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Northwest Ya'Ao Information Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at: B26/F, Shengtingyuan, Huaqiang North Road, Futian District, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Yuming, General Manager of the Company.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Wuzhong Instrument Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at: No. 67, Chaoyang Street, Wuzhong City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Shenzhen Guo'an Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd., domiciled at: 12/F, South China Electric Power Building, No. 2050, Shennan Middle Road, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Zhenhai, Director of the Company.

The appellant, Shenzhen Commercial Bank, Bao'an Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Bao'an Sub-branch), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2006) Xiang Gao Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 1 rendered by the Hunan High People's Court in the dispute over return of funds and guarantee contracts with the appellees, Hunan Changlian Xingchang Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xingchang Company), Shenzhen Minxin Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Minxin Company), Guangdong Jinhuiyuan Investment Guarantee Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinhuiyuan Company), Northwest Ya'Ao Information Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Northwest Ya'Ao Company), Wuzhong Instrument Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Wuzhong Instrument Company), and Shenzhen Guo'an Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guo'an Accounting Firm). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Presiding Judge Qian Xiaochen, and Acting Judges Liu Min and Yang Zhengyu participating in the trial, and Court Clerk Yuan Hongxia taking the record. The case is now concluded.

The following facts were found upon trial by the Hunan High People's Court:

On August 17, 2001, Xingchang Company and Minxin Company entered into an "Entrusted Asset Management Contract," stipulating that Xingchang Company entrusted Minxin Company with the management of assets totaling RMB 40 million, with a contract term of one year, from August 17, 2001 to August 16, 2002. Xingchang Company opened a special account at the Shenzhen Securities Business Department of Qinghai Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department) designated by Minxin Company, and entrusted Minxin Company with the management of the aforesaid assets. On the same day, Xingchang Company, Minxin Company, and Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department signed a "Supplementary Agreement to the Entrusted Asset Management Contract," stipulating that Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department was responsible for supervising Xingchang Company's assets of RMB 40 million. On August 21 and 22 of the same month, Xingchang Company remitted funds totaling RMB 40 million in seven installments (RMB 12 million, RMB 3 million, RMB 2 million, RMB 1 million, RMB 8 million, RMB 5 million, and RMB 9 million, respectively) to Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department, which issued a "Guarantee Deposit Slip" for RMB 40 million deposited into the account numbered 824040 under the name of Xingchang Company. After the expiration of the said contract, Xingchang Company and Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department signed a "Cooperation Agreement" on August 18, 2002, stipulating that Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department would establish a guarantee deposit account of RMB 40 million in the name of Xingchang Company, with Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department assuming supervisory responsibilities.

On November 16 of the same year, Xingchang Company, in the name of its subordinate unit Changlian Xingchang Yueyang LPG Station (hereinafter referred to as Yueyang LPG Station), remitted funds totaling RMB 10 million in three installments (RMB 3 million, RMB 3 million, and RMB 4 million, respectively) to Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department. On November 18 of the same month, it signed a "Cooperation Agreement" with Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department, stipulating that Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department would establish a guarantee deposit account of RMB 10 million in the name of Xingchang Company, with Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department assuming supervisory responsibilities. The annual return rate for Xingchang Company's deposits with Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department was 0.99%. Xingchang Company received returns quarterly from Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department, with the payment date being the 18th day of the last month of each quarter, and interest calculated from the date Xingchang Company's guarantee deposit arrived at Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department. Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department guaranteed the safety of Xingchang Company's funds and, upon expiration of the cooperation period, would pay the guarantee deposit and interest to Xingchang Company. The contract term was from November 18, 2001 to November 18, 2002. On the same day, Xingchang Company, Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department, and Minxin Company signed a "Supplementary Agreement" to the "Cooperation Agreement." On November 19 of the same month, Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department issued a "Guarantee Deposit Slip" for RMB 10 million deposited into the account numbered 824128 under the name of Wan Mingzhu.

On January 16, 2002, Xingchang Company again, in the name of Yueyang LPG Station, remitted funds totaling RMB 80 million in a single installment to Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department. On January 17 of the same month, Xingchang Company issued a "Certificate" to Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department, stating that Yueyang LPG Station was a subordinate unit of the company and that the account numbered 824128 under the name of Wan Mingzhu belonged to the company. On January 18 of the same month, Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department issued a "Guarantee Deposit Slip" for RMB 80 million deposited into the account numbered 824128 under the name of Wan Mingzhu.

After the three "Cooperation Agreements" successively expired at the end of the same year, neither Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department nor Minxin Company returned the aforesaid funds to Xingchang Company.

On January 1, 2003, Xingchang Company and Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department signed an "Entrusted Asset Management Agreement," stipulating that the existing funds of RMB 130 million in the guarantee deposit account opened by Xingchang Company in the name of Xingchang Company at Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department would serve as guarantee deposits, managed by Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department. On the same day, Xingchang Company, Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department, and Minxin Company signed a "Supplementary Agreement to the Entrusted Asset Management Agreement," stipulating that all economic losses arising from the said guarantee deposit account opened by Xingchang Company at Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department would be borne by Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department. On December 31 of the same year, the said "Entrusted Asset Management Agreement" again reached its maturity date, and Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department and Minxin Company were still unable to return the funds to Xingchang Company.

On January 1, 2004, Xingchang Company, Minxin Company, and Jinhuiyuan Company entered into a "Debt Repayment Agreement," stipulating that Xingchang Company agreed to extend the repayment of the overdue guarantee deposit principal of RMB 130 million owed by Minxin Company to September 30, 2004, with the guarantor Jinhuiyuan Company assuming joint and several guarantee liability. If the debt remained unpaid after the extension, Xingchang Company had the right to demand full payment from either Minxin Company or Jinhuiyuan Company. Minxin Company agreed to calculate interest at an annual rate of 11% on the guarantee deposit principal of RMB 130 million as Xingchang Company's return. At the same time, Xingchang Company agreed that Minxin Company could repay the RMB 130 million principal owed to Xingchang Company in installments before September 30, 2004, with the balance after each partial repayment serving as the base for calculating returns; the returns obtained were to be paid quarterly by Minxin Company, and Jinhuiyuan Company assumed joint and several guarantee liability for the said returns. If by September 30, 2004, Minxin Company still failed to repay the guarantee deposit, it would pay Xingchang Company an additional daily penalty at a rate of 0.04% of the unpaid amount, and Jinhuiyuan Company assumed joint and several guarantee liability for this part of the penalty. Pursuant to the said "Debt Repayment Agreement," Jinhuiyuan Company and Xingchang Company signed a "Guarantee Contract" on the same day.

Separately, it was found that in January 2003, Qinghai Securities Co., Ltd. changed its name to Kunlun Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kunlun Securities Company). The Shenzhen Securities Business Department of Qinghai Securities was cancelled on August 11, 2003.

On December 18 of the same year, Jinhuiyuan Company, in accordance with a shareholders' resolution and its articles of association, decided to increase its registered capital from RMB 50 million to RMB 300 million, with the additional capital contributed by the original shareholder Northwest Ya'Ao Company in the amount of RMB 150 million, the new shareholder Gansu Securities Co., Ltd. subscribing RMB 50 million, and the new shareholder Wuzhong Instrument Company subscribing RMB 50 million. On January 5, 2004, Northwest Ya'Ao Company applied to change the registered capital of Jinhuiyuan Company from RMB 50 million to RMB 300 million, and the change registration was completed. However, an inquiry by the Yueyang Yunxi District People's Court of Hunan Province on March 8, 2005, into the account numbered 0282100346110 opened by Jinhuiyuan Company at Bao'an Sub-branch for the purpose of increasing registered capital showed that no transactions had occurred in this account before January 6, 2004, confirming that Northwest Ya'Ao Company had not actually made the additional capital contribution of RMB 150 million, and Wuzhong Instrument Company had not made its capital contribution of RMB 50 million. On February 6, 2004, Bao'an Sub-branch issued a capital verification certificate indicating that Jinhuiyuan Company had a deposit of RMB 250 million in account numbered 0282100346110 at Bao'an Sub-branch. On the same day, Guo'an Accounting Firm issued a capital verification report stating that Jinhuiyuan Company had received the new registered capital contributions of RMB 150 million, RMB 50 million, and RMB 50 million from Northwest Ya'Ao Company, Wuzhong Instrument Company, and Gansu Securities Co., Ltd., respectively.

On November 23, 2005, Xingchang Company filed a lawsuit with the Hunan High People's Court, requesting a judgment ordering Minxin Company and Kunlun Securities Company to return RMB 130 million and interest, and to bear joint and several supplementary compensatory liability; Jinhuiyuan Company to assume joint and several guarantee liability for Minxin Company's obligations; and the three defendants to jointly bear the litigation costs. On December 30 of the same year, Xingchang Company applied to withdraw its claim against Kunlun Securities Company, and the Hunan High People's Court granted the withdrawal. On the same day, Xingchang Company submitted a supplementary complaint to the Hunan High People's Court, adding Northwest Ya'Ao Company, Wuzhong Instrument Company, Guo'an Accounting Firm, and Bao'an Sub-branch as co-defendants in the case, requesting a judgment ordering Northwest Ya'Ao Company and Wuzhong Instrument Company to bear civil liability within the range of their false capital contributions of RMB 200 million; and Guo'an Accounting Firm and Bao'an Sub-branch to bear supplementary civil liability within the range of the false capital verification report and false capital verification certificate of RMB 200 million they issued; and the supplementary defendants to bear the litigation costs and all other reasonable expenses of the case.

The court of first instance held that the "Entrusted Asset Management Contract" between Xingchang Company and Minxin Company, the "Cooperation Agreement" between Xingchang Company and Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department, and the "Supplementary Agreement to the Entrusted Asset Management Contract" signed by Xingchang Company, Minxin Company, and Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department, as viewed from the business scope approved on the business license issued to Minxin Company by the Administration for Industry and Commerce, which limited its business to the production and operation of electronic components and plastic hardware products (excluding restricted items), did not grant Minxin Company any financial qualification. Pursuant to Article 10 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (I), contracts entered into by a company beyond its business scope must not violate the state's provisions on restricted operations, franchising, or prohibitions on operations under laws and administrative regulations. The said "Entrusted Asset Management Contract," "Cooperation Agreement," and "Supplementary Agreement to the Entrusted Asset Management Contract" were invalid as they violated mandatory state prohibitions. Since the said contracts were invalid, Minxin Company should return the entrusted managed funds of RMB 130 million to Xingchang Company. The "Debt Repayment Agreement" subsequently reached between Minxin Company and Xingchang Company regarding the said entrusted funds represented a new arrangement for the return of the entrusted funds. This agreement reflected the true intention of the parties, its content did not violate prohibitive provisions of laws or regulations, and it was a valid and effective contract. However, the high-return interest stipulated in the "Debt Repayment Agreement" violated relevant legal provisions, and the portion exceeding lawful interest was not protected. Since Minxin Company failed to fulfill its obligation to return the funds as agreed in the "Debt Repayment Agreement," it constituted a breach of contract. Therefore, Xingchang Company's claim for Minxin Company to return RMB 130 million and corresponding interest should be upheld.

Jinhuiyuan Company signed and sealed the "Debt Repayment Agreement" between Xingchang Company and Minxin Company as a guarantor, and on the same day signed a "Guarantee Contract" with Xingchang Company, stipulating that Jinhuiyuan Company assumed joint and several guarantee liability for the RMB 130 million owed by Minxin Company to Xingchang Company, as well as the payable returns and costs of realizing the claims. Pursuant to Article 18 of the Guarantee Law, Xingchang Company's claim for Jinhuiyuan Company to assume joint and several guarantee liability for the RMB 130 million and corresponding interest owed by Minxin Company to Xingchang Company was lawful and should be upheld.

On December 18, 2003, in accordance with the shareholders' resolution and the articles of association, Jinhuiyuan Company decided to increase its registered capital from RMB 50 million to RMB 300 million. The additional capital was to be contributed by the original shareholder Northwest Ya'Ao Company in the amount of RMB 150 million, with new shareholder Gansu Securities Co., Ltd. subscribing RMB 50 million, and new shareholder Wuzhong Instrument Company subscribing RMB 50 million. On January 5, 2004, Jinhuiyuan Company's registered capital was changed in the industry and commerce registration from RMB 50 million to RMB 300 million. According to the inquiry by the Yueyang Yunxi District People's Court of Hunan Province on March 8, 2005, into account numbered 0282100346110 opened by Jinhuiyuan Company at Bao'an Sub-branch for the purpose of increasing registered capital, it was confirmed that no transactions had occurred in this account before January 6, 2004, proving that Northwest Ya'Ao Company had not actually made the additional capital contribution of RMB 150 million, and Wuzhong Instrument Company had not actually made its capital contribution of RMB 50 million. Pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Company Law, when a company registers an increase in its registered capital, the shareholders subscribing to the registered capital must pay the subscribed amounts truthfully. In this case, when Jinhuiyuan Company applied for the change registration of its registered capital, the original shareholder Northwest Ya'Ao Company and the new shareholder Wuzhong Instrument Company did not contribute the capital they had committed to in accordance with the articles of association and the shareholders' resolution. Therefore, they should bear supplementary liability for the company's external debts to the extent of their insufficient capital contributions. Accordingly, Xingchang Company's claim that Northwest Ya'Ao Company and Wuzhong Instrument Company should bear supplementary compensation liability for Jinhuiyuan Company's debts within the scope of their false capital contributions was in accordance with the law and should be upheld.

Based on the testimony of Ruan Hao, the handler of the bank confirmation letter from Bao'an Sub-branch, and the fact that Bao'an Sub-branch charged a confirmation fee of RMB 30, it indicated that the bank confirmation letter originated from Bao'an Sub-branch. Bao'an Sub-branch argued that the official seals affixed to the bank confirmation letter and the bank debit note were forged by others, and thus it should not be held liable in this case. However, from the existing evidence, even if the seal on those documents was inconsistent with the seal specimen provided by Bao'an Sub-branch, this does not prove that the sub-branch used only one seal. Moreover, the sub-branch's employee Liu Shaoping, as the person in charge, participated in the business activity of issuing the bank confirmation letter, and Bao'an Sub-branch should bear the legal consequences arising therefrom. Therefore, this defense of Bao'an Sub-branch was untenable and was not accepted by the court. As to the issue that the timing of the guarantee contract between Xingchang Company and Jinhuiyuan Company was after the bank issued the capital verification certificate and after Guo'an Accounting Firm issued the capital verification report, since the Shenzhen Administration for Industry and Commerce had already issued a new business license to Jinhuiyuan Company on January 5, 2004, the bank's issuance of the capital verification certificate and Guo'an Accounting Firm's issuance of the capital verification report on February 6, 2004, should be considered as supplementary capital verification acts. Moreover, the staff of Guo'an Accounting Firm also confirmed that they were required by the Shenzhen Administration for Industry and Commerce to go through the procedures for issuing a supplementary capital verification report. Therefore, even if the capital verification certificate and the capital verification report were issued after the signing of the guarantee contract, they should be deemed to have been used. Additionally, when Xingchang Company and Jinhuiyuan Company signed the guarantee contract on January 1, 2004, Jinhuiyuan Company's articles of association had already been amended to reflect the increased registered capital from Northwest Ya'Ao Company and Wuzhong Instrument Company, and the shareholders' resolution had also been passed. Based on this, Xingchang Company had reason to believe that the new registered capital would be fully paid when it signed the guarantee contract. Therefore, Xingchang Company acted in good faith and without fault when signing the guarantee contract. Bao'an Sub-branch, by issuing a false capital verification certificate when the new registered capital had not been paid, harmed the interests of Jinhuiyuan Company's creditors, and should bear supplementary compensation liability in accordance with the law.

The existing evidence shows that Guo'an Accounting Firm did not violate any professional rules during the capital verification process. The authenticity of the capital verification certificate relied upon by Guo'an Accounting Firm in issuing its capital verification report should be the responsibility of the issuing bank, Bao'an Sub-branch. Therefore, Guo'an Accounting Firm should not bear compensation liability in this case. As for Xingchang Company's claim in its supplementary complaint for the supplementary defendants to bear other litigation costs, since no corresponding evidence was submitted, the court did not uphold this claim.

In summary, pursuant to Article 84 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 18 of the Guaranty Law of the People's Republic of China, and paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court Notice No. [2002] 21 on Issues Concerning the Civil Liability of Financial Institutions for Issuing Untruthful or False Capital Verification Reports or Capital Certificates for Enterprises, the court rendered the following judgment: 1. Minxin Company shall, within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, return RMB 130 million and corresponding interest to Xingchang Company (interest calculated from January 1, 2004, at the bank deposit interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period until the date of full payment); 2. Jinhuiyuan Company shall bear joint and several liability for the repayment of the above amount by Minxin Company; 3. To the extent that Minxin Company and Jinhuiyuan Company are unable to repay the above amount, Xibei Ya'ao Company shall bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of RMB 150 million; 4. To the extent that Minxin Company and Jinhuiyuan Company are unable to repay the above amount, Wuzhong Instrument Company shall bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of RMB 50 million; 5. To the extent that Xibei Ya'ao Company and Wuzhong Instrument Company are still unable to repay the above amount, Bao'an Sub-branch shall bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of RMB 200 million; after bearing liability, Bao'an Sub-branch may seek recourse from Jinhuiyuan Company; 6. Xingchang Company's claim against Guoan Accounting Firm was dismissed; 7. Xingchang Company's other claims were dismissed. The case acceptance fee was RMB 660,010, and the property preservation fee was RMB 250,520, totaling RMB 910,530, to be borne by Minxin Company.

Bao'an Sub-branch, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Hunan High People's Court, appealed to this Court, arguing: According to the appellant's operational procedures for inquiry and verification business, Xingchang Company cannot prove whether the inquirer received the capital certificate or that the capital certificate submitted as evidence was issued by the appellant, and cannot rule out the possibility that the inquirer forged or altered the genuine capital certificate issued by the appellant. There is no necessary connection between the appellant's collection of an inquiry fee of RMB 30 and the so-called capital certificate. The "Statement of Facts" issued by Ruan Hao, a former partner of Guoan Accounting Firm, was provided by a person with a fundamental interest in the case, was not submitted within the evidence submission period, and was not cross-examined; thus it cannot be used as evidence. The court of first instance's acquisition and use of this evidence seriously violated the rules of evidence in civil proceedings. The seals affixed to all capital certificates submitted by Xingchang Company as allegedly issued by the appellant were forgeries. When the court of first instance discovered during trial that the evidence provided by the appellant sufficiently proved that the seals on the so-called capital certificates were forgeries, it actually prevented cross-examination in court, violating legal provisions. Moreover, even if the appellant had issued the so-called capital certificate in this case, since Xingchang Company accepted Jinhuiyuan Company's guarantee before the alleged issuance of the capital certificate by the appellant, Xingchang Company could not have relied on a capital certificate not yet issued by the appellant as the basis for accepting the guarantee. From the guarantee company's articles of association and shareholders' resolution, there was no fact of deemed use of the capital certificate. There was no causal relationship between Xingchang Company's acceptance of Jinhuiyuan Company's guarantee and the alleged capital certificate issued by the appellant. Xingchang Company's knowledge that Jinhuiyuan Company had amended its articles of association and that the shareholders' resolution had been adopted occurred after Xingchang Company filed the lawsuit, not at the time of signing the "Repayment Agreement." Xingchang Company had no evidence that it used the capital certificate issued by the appellant and suffered loss; therefore, the appellant cannot bear liability for this. Qinghai Securities Shenzhen Business Department is the direct obligor for repayment of the funds. The "Repayment Agreement" signed between Xingchang Company and Minxin Company and the guarantee agreement signed with Jinhuiyuan Company are invalid. The court of first instance erred in finding that Minxin Company was the obligor for the funds involved in the case and in ordering Jinhuiyuan Company to bear guarantee liability for a non-existent debt, thereby ordering the appellant to bear supplementary compensation liability. The judgment of first instance erred in fact-finding and improperly applied the law. The appellant requested that paragraph 5 of the judgment of first instance be revoked and that Xingchang Company bear the appellant's appeal fees and attorney fees.

The appellee Xingchang Company responded: As a regular financial institution, Bao'an Sub-branch should retain copies or relevant records for the issuance of important capital certificates. Bao'an Sub-branch failed to provide relevant evidence to prove that the inquirer did not receive the capital certificate after paying fees or that it issued a genuine capital certificate. Bao'an Sub-branch was obligated to submit evidence retained and filed related to the collection of inquiry fees. Bao'an Sub-branch failed to prove the uniqueness of its seal, and therefore there is no evidence that the capital certificate involved in this case was forged or altered. The seal impression submitted by Bao'an Sub-branch was not produced by a third party qualified to retain its seal impression; it was a unilateral act and lacks evidentiary effect. The court of first instance has already found that the seal on the capital certificate did not match the seal impression submitted by Bao'an Sub-branch, so no further authentication was needed. The court of first instance did not organize evidence exchange; relevant evidence was excerpted or copied by the parties from the collegiate bench's files. Bao'an Sub-branch's failure to excerpt or copy this evidence was not a procedural violation by the court. The court of first instance submitted the investigation record of Ruan Hao to both parties for cross-examination. Since Ruan Hao conducted business in the name of Guoan Accounting Firm, it is reasonable that he did not know the names of the persons handling business for Jinhuiyuan Company. When Jinhuiyuan Company registered its capital increase, although the business license was issued before the supplementary capital verification, the issuance of the business license actually occurred after the capital verification, so it did not violate the relevant provisions on company registration. The losses suffered by the respondent in economic dealings with Minxin Company and others were based on trust in the capital certificate issued by the financial institution. The guarantee contract specifically provided that the respondent had the right to supervise Jinhuiyuan Company's funds and property, and to require Jinhuiyuan Company to provide recent financial statements audited by an accounting firm engaged by itself, which Jinhuiyuan Company was required to provide truthfully. The purpose of this clause was to ensure the performance of the guarantee obligation. Before the guarantee contract was signed, Jinhuiyuan Company had shareholders' resolutions and board resolutions for capital increase and share expansion. After the guarantee contract was signed, Jinhuiyuan Company conducted capital verification and audit for the capital increase and share expansion within the relevant time to perfect the change registration; this constituted use of the capital verification certificate. After Jinhuiyuan Company received the new business license, it again commissioned Guoan Accounting Firm to issue a capital verification report, which provided clear capital confirmation for its guarantee obligation. The guarantee obligation only begins after the guarantee fact occurs. Bao'an Sub-branch's capital certificate was issued after the guarantee contract was signed but before the guarantee obligation was undertaken, confirming that the guarantor indeed had the qualification to bear the guarantee obligation. Therefore, it can definitely be concluded that the guarantee contract in this case actually used the capital certificate. Minxin Company is the true entrusted asset manager. The repayment agreement and guarantee contract signed between Xingchang Company, Minxin Company, and Jinhuiyuan Company reflected the true intentions of the parties and are lawful and valid. The judgment of first instance had clear fact-finding, lawful procedures, and correct application of law. The appellee requested that the appeal be dismissed and the judgment of first instance be affirmed.

The other appellees did not submit defense opinions.

This Court affirms the facts found by the court of first instance, except for the fact that Bao'an Sub-branch issued a capital certificate on February 6, 2004.

Opinion of the Court: The main issue in dispute in this appeal is whether Bao'an Sub-branch should bear compensation liability for issuing a false capital certificate in relation to Jinhuiyuan Company's guarantee debt to Xingchang Company. On January 1, 2004, Xingchang Company, Minxin Company, and Jinhuiyuan Company signed a repayment agreement concerning Minxin Company's overdue margin principal of RMB 130 million owed to Xingchang Company, and Jinhuiyuan Company provided a guarantee for the repayment of this amount. On January 5 of the same year, Jinhuiyuan Company changed its registered capital in the industrial and commercial register from the original RMB 50 million to RMB 300 million. During the trial of first instance, the relevant parties submitted a bank inquiry letter dated February 6 of the same year, bearing the official seal of Bao'an Sub-branch. This inquiry letter stated that on February 6, Jinhuiyuan Company's shareholders, Xibei Ya'ao Company, Wuzhong Instrument Company, and Qinghai Securities Co., Ltd., had deposited a total of RMB 250 million in investment capital into account number 0282100346110 of Jinhuiyuan Company at Bao'an Sub-branch. However, upon verification by the relevant court, the above capital certificate was false, and Jinhuiyuan Company's additional registered capital had not actually been paid in. Whether Bao'an Sub-branch should bear compensation liability for issuing the false capital certificate depends on whether it actually issued the above false capital certificate bearing its seal, and whether Xingchang Company's losses resulting from Jinhuiyuan Company's provision of the guarantee were caused by reasonable reliance on or use of Bao'an Sub-branch's false capital certificate. That is, whether Bao'an Sub-branch committed a tort in this case and whether there is a causal relationship between Xingchang Company's losses and Bao'an Sub-branch's tort are key to determining whether Bao'an Sub-branch should bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of the false capital verification when Xibei Ya'ao Company and Wuzhong Instrument Company, the two shareholders of Jinhuiyuan Company with defective capital contributions, cannot bear liability for such defective contributions. Given that the bank inquiry letter bearing Bao'an Sub-branch's seal had not yet been issued when Xingchang Company and Jinhuiyuan Company signed the guarantee contract, Xingchang Company did not sign the guarantee contract based on reliance on the content of the additional capital contributions stated in that bank inquiry letter. There is no necessary causal relationship between Xingchang Company's losses arising from the inability to fully realize the guarantee obligation due to Jinhuiyuan Company's defective additional capital contributions and the bank inquiry letter bearing Bao'an Sub-branch's seal. When Xingchang Company and Jinhuiyuan Company signed the guarantee contract, although Jinhuiyuan Company's articles of association and shareholders' resolution had already recorded and resolved the additional capital contributions, the recording in the articles of association and the adoption of the shareholders' resolution have no bearing on whether Bao'an Sub-branch should bear compensation liability. Xingchang Company should have signed the guarantee contract based on its reliance on Jinhuiyuan Company, not on reliance on the capital certificate bearing Bao'an Sub-branch's seal. Therefore, Xingchang Company's claim that Bao'an Sub-branch should bear corresponding compensation liability for Xibei Ya'ao Company and Wuzhong Instrument Company's defective capital contribution liability lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it. The court of first instance's finding that Bao'an Sub-branch's issuance of the capital certificate constituted supplementary capital verification and should be deemed used even if issued after the guarantee contract was signed was improper, and this Court corrects it. This Court supports Bao'an Sub-branch's appeal request that there was no causal relationship between Xingchang Company's signing of the guarantee contract with Jinhuiyuan Company and the capital certificate bearing Bao'an Sub-branch's seal, and that it should not bear liability for issuing the false capital contribution certificate in this case. As to whether the capital certificate bearing Bao'an Sub-branch's seal was actually issued by Bao'an Sub-branch and whether the seal was forged, since this does not affect this Court's determination that Bao'an Sub-branch does not bear liability for Xingchang Company's debt in this case, this Court will no longer review these issues. If the above capital certificate was indeed issued by Bao'an Sub-branch, although it does not bear liability for this debt, this does not naturally exempt it from other compensation liabilities arising from the issuance of such false capital certificate. Bao'an Sub-branch's other appeal grounds, such as the claim that Minxin Company is not the debtor of the debt in this case, also do not affect this Court's determination that it does not bear compensation liability in this case, and this Court will also no longer review them. Bao'an Sub-branch's appeal request that Xingchang Company bear its attorney fees is not supported by this Court. In summary, pursuant to Article 106, paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 153, paragraph 1, item (2) and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court renders the following judgment:

1. Items 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 7 of the civil judgment (2006) Xiang Gao Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 1 of the Hunan High People's Court, as well as the portion concerning the litigation costs, are affirmed;
2. Item 5 of the above civil judgment is reversed;
3. Other appeal requests of Shenzhen Commercial Bank Bao'an Sub-branch are dismissed.

If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The appeal acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 660,010, to be borne by Hunan Changlian Xingchang Group Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
